title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: González (1985) algorithm builds selection greedily: start seed point, repeatedly add whichever unselected point farthest current selection. greedy rule guarantees 2-approximation optimal Tk runs O(N · m) time. default FarFirst() runs three "random_furthest" starts, beginning point furthest randomly selected ‘pivot’ point, returns whichever pass produced highest Tk. random starts, pivots devising, can accomplished vector pivot points pivots vector. Peripheral seeds may also selected deterministic methods: one methods can selected via seed argument. best solution found returned. pairwise distances objects known — coordinates work — computing storing N×N distances expensive, function may passed place distance matrix. function passed one index , returns distances object N objects — one column matrix. FarFirst() calls nn times, full N×N matrix never built. N, number objects, must supplied.
code: set.seed(1) picks <- FarFirst(eurodist, n = 6L)   # default: best of three random starts set.seed(1) nCities <- attr(eurodist, "Size") # Use 5 random starts pivots <- sample(nCities, 5) picks <- FarFirst(eurodist, n = 6L, pivots = pivots) picks <- FarFirst(eurodist, n = 6L, seed = c("diameter", "anti_medoid")) MinDist(eurodist, picks) #> [1] 1014  attr(picks, "winning_strategy") #> [1] "diameter"    "anti_medoid" data("USArrests") arrestTypes <- USArrests[, c("Murder", "Assault", "Rape")] StateDist <- function(i) {   diffs <- sweep(arrestTypes, 2, unlist(arrestTypes[i, ]), "-")   sqrt(rowSums(diffs ^ 2)) } idx <- FarFirst(StateDist, n = 4L, N = nrow(arrestTypes), seed = 1L) arrestTypes[idx, ] #>                Murder Assault Rape #> Alabama          13.2     236 21.2 #> North Dakota      0.8      45  7.3 #> North Carolina   13.0     337 16.1 #> Washington        4.0     145 26.2

title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: DropAdd heuristic (Porumbel et al., 2011) refines initial selection alternately dropping adding points selection; typically reaches ≈ 99 % optimal Tk. algorithm terminates plateau iterations improve Tk. N large distance matrix fit memory (roughly N > 46 000), pass coordinate matrix via DropAdd(points = ...).
code: picksDA <- DropAdd(eurodist, m = 6L, plateau = 500L)  labels(eurodist)[picksDA] #> [1] "Athens"    "Barcelona" "Cherbourg" "Lisbon"    "Stockholm" "Vienna" attr(picksDA, "score")  # T_k achieved #> [1] 1294 attr(picksDA, "iters")      # iterations completed #> [1] 516 attr(picksDA, "time_s")     # wall-clock seconds #> [1] 0.0002551079

title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: GRASP + path relinking (Resende et al., 2010) combines randomised greedy construction phase extended local search refines elite set good solutions interpolating elite-pair trajectories (path relinking). achieves highest Tk three heuristics, proportionally higher cost. construction phase stochastic, always set seed reproducibility: plateau controls many consecutive non-improving GRASP iterations trigger termination; timeBudgetS available absolute time cap interactive batch use.
code: res_gr <- GraspPR(eurodist, m = 6L, plateau = 50L, seed = 42L)  labels(eurodist)[res_gr] #> [1] "Athens"    "Barcelona" "Calais"    "Lisbon"    "Stockholm" "Vienna" attr(res_gr, "score") #> [1] 1305 attr(res_gr, "pr_calls")   # path-relinking calls performed #> [1] 90

what: Comparing methods on a simulated example
title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: see methods relate visually, generate 50 points two dimensions select m = 8 . Even small difference Tk can correspond meaningfully dispersed selection. Plotting selections point cloud makes differences concrete. two methods select index, symbols overlap; Tk table captures quality distinction even visual overlap high.  Selections returned method 50 random 2-D points (m = 8). Coloured symbols mark selected points; grey circles full candidate set. small jitter separates symbols shared indices.
code: set.seed(42) pts <- matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2)   # 50 points, 2 dimensions d50 <- dist(pts) m   <- 8L idx_ff <- FarFirst(d50, n = m) res_da50 <- DropAdd(d50, m = m, plateau = 500L) res_gr50 <- GraspPR(d50, m = m, plateau = 50L, seed = 42L) scores <- c(   FarFirst  = MinDist(d50, idx_ff),   DropAdd = attr(res_da50, "score"),   GraspPR   = attr(res_gr50, "score") ) round(scores, 3) #> FarFirst  DropAdd  GraspPR  #>    1.416    1.428    1.428 methods <- list(   FarFirst  = idx_ff,   DropAdd = res_da50,   GraspPR   = res_gr50 ) cols <- c(FarFirst = "#E41A1C", DropAdd = "#377EB8", GraspPR = "#4DAF4A") pchs <- c(FarFirst = 24L, DropAdd = 21L, GraspPR = 22L) # Small per-method shift so coincident selections remain distinguishable dx   <- c(FarFirst = 0, DropAdd =  0.04, GraspPR = -0.04) dy   <- c(FarFirst = 0, DropAdd = -0.04, GraspPR =  0.04)  plot(pts, pch = 1L, col = "grey75", asp = 1L,      xlab = "x", ylab = "y",      main = "MaxMin method comparison")  for (nm in names(methods)) {   sel <- methods[[nm]]   points(     pts[sel, 1L] + dx[nm],     pts[sel, 2L] + dy[nm],     pch = pchs[nm], col = cols[nm], bg = cols[nm], cex = 1.6   ) }  legend("topright",        legend = paste0(names(methods), "  (Tₖ = ", round(scores, 3), ")"),        pch = pchs, col = cols, pt.bg = cols, pt.cex = 1.4, bty = "n")

title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: small instances (roughly N ≤ 25–30), ExactMaxMin() solves problem proven optimality via node-packing integer programme (Sayyady & Fathi, 2016), using highs solver. First must install highs: $proven = TRUE certifies selection can achieve higher Tk. ExactMaxMin() NP-hard; instances ~30 candidates require time budget tackled heuristics .
code: install.packages("highs") set.seed(1L) pts30 <- matrix(rnorm(60L), ncol = 2L) d30   <- dist(pts30) res_ex <- ExactMaxMin(d30, m = 6L, timeBudgetS = 30L)  res_ex$proven      # TRUE  ⟹  objective is the global optimum #> [1] TRUE res_ex$objective #> [1] 1.616311  # Compare to the greedy heuristic on the same instance res_ff30 <- FarFirst(d30, n = 6L) c(exact    = res_ex$objective,   Gonzalez = MinDist(d30, res_ff30)) #>    exact Gonzalez  #> 1.616311 1.616311

title: DropAdd Tabu Search for the Max-Min Diversity Problem — DropAdd
text: d dist object square symmetric numeric matrix. Mutually exclusive points; supply exactly one. m Integer; subset size, \(2 \le m \le n\). plateau Integer; stop many consecutive drop-add iterations improve best objective. primary, deterministic stopping criterion. search RNG-free (ties broken smallest index), given instance result reproducible machine-independent. Default 5000. maxIter Optional integer hard cap iterations (excluding construction). NULL (default) leaves plateau sole control. timeBudgetS Optional wall-clock ceiling seconds, checked iteration boundaries. Default Inf (ceiling, fully reproducible). finite value caps runtime makes result machine-dependent. seed Optional integer; non-NULL, set.seed(seed) called entry. algorithm deterministic ties (broken smallest index), seed observable effect solution; exposed API parity stochastic methods. progress Logical; show start/done status line. Default: TRUE interactive sessions, FALSE otherwise (getOption("MaxMin.progress", interactive())). effect .verify = TRUE (testing path). points numeric \(n \times \mathrm{dim}\) coordinate matrix (object coercible one via .matrix). Must complete (NA). Mutually exclusive d; supply exactly one. supplied, algorithm never materialises dense \(n \times n\) distance matrix, giving \(O(n)\) working memory enabling use \(n\) far exceeding matrix path's ceiling (R's .matrix.dist overflows \(n = 46340\)). .verify Logical (testing ); TRUE, routes R reference loop brute-force asserts streamlined records every iteration. Default FALSE (C++ fast path). applies d path. .trace Optional environment (testing ); supplied, dropped added index sequences written drops adds.

title: DropAdd Tabu Search for the Max-Min Diversity Problem — DropAdd
text: integer vector length m containing 1-based selected indices (sorted ascending), attributes: score numeric(1), achieved MaxMin objective \(\min_{\ne j \S} d_{ij}\). secondary numeric(1), achieved sum pairwise distances \(S\) (upper-triangle sum). time_s numeric(1), wall-clock seconds spent. iters integer(1), main-loop iterations executed (excluding construction phase).

title: DropAdd Tabu Search for the Max-Min Diversity Problem — DropAdd
text: MMDPo objective optimised $$\min_{x,y \X} d(x,y) + \epsilon \sum_{x,y \X} d(x,y),$$ \(\epsilon = 10^{-9}\), pairwise sum acts tie-break. Tabu mechanics. algorithm maintains integer iter stamp every point, set iteration point last entered left selected set \(X\). main-loop iteration point smallest iter value (oldest member, FIFO) dropped, point \(Z \setminus X\) maximising lexicographically \((\mathrm{minDist}, \mathrm{sumDist})\) added. FIFO invariant guarantees across window \(m\) iterations every initially-selected point dropped exactly re-eviction.

title: Deterministic Gonzalez furthest-point selection — FarFirst
text: Greedy k-centre selection (González 1985) . Iteratively selects point furthest current selection, 2-approximation k-centre problem. quality result depends first (seed) point; default FarFirst() runs three starts randomly selected peripheral seeds. deterministic O(N) anchors ("centroid", "peripheral") costlier O(N^2) anchors ("diameter", "anti_medoid", "medoid", "rowsum", "rownorm") alternative seed strategies.

title: Deterministic Gonzalez furthest-point selection — FarFirst
text: d dist object, square symmetric numeric matrix pairwise distances, distance function (see §Distance function). Ignored points supplied. n Integer: number points select. n >= N, indices returned. seed Integer character (scalar vector). integer gives explicit 1-based index first selected point (single bare Gonzalez pass). length-1 character names single deterministic seeding strategy run one bare pass: "centroid" (coordinates ), "peripheral" (two-sweep diameter-endpoint approximation), "diameter", "anti_medoid", "medoid", "rowsum", "rownorm", "first" (index 1). length > 1 character vector – lone "random_furthest" token – requests ensemble: named anchor runs full Gonzalez pass best result MinDist() returned strategy_results winning_strategy (character vector tied-best strategies) attributes. "random_furthest" token expands one start per element pivots, labelled random_furthest1, random_furthest2, ...; named still runs ensemble (one pass per pivot), single random start best obtained via MaxMinSeed(). Valid ensemble anchors: subset c("centroid", "peripheral", "random_furthest", "diameter", "anti_medoid", "medoid", "rowsum", "rownorm") ("centroid" requires points). Default: "random_furthest" (three random starts; see pivots). See MaxMinSeed() anchor definitions. distance-column oracle path integer seed honoured; named ensemble seed warns falls back peripheral seed (see Distance-column oracle). pivots Integer vector pivot indices "random_furthest" ensemble token expands: pivot contributes one start, seeded point furthest , vector's length sets number random-furthest starts. Left unspecified, three pivots drawn session RNG (sample.int(N, 3); set seed reproducible selection). Pass integer(0), NA, NULL disable random starts, index vector choose pivots (count) explicitly. Disabling random starts errors default seed (names "random_furthest", leaving anchor); pair deterministic seed "peripheral". points Optional N x dim numeric coordinate matrix. supplied, selection computed directly coordinates O(N * n * dim) time O(N) memory, never materialising N x N distance matrix (d unused). Euclidean data returned indices identical matrix path. complete (non-NA) data supported. N Integer: total number elements. Required (used) distance-column oracle path, inferred closure; ignored matrix coordinate paths. progress Logical; show progress bar greedy selection distance-column oracle path (path slow enough warrant one). Default: TRUE interactive sessions, FALSE otherwise (getOption("MaxMin.progress", interactive())).

title: MaxMin 0.0.0.9000 (development)
text: Initial release: tiered toolbox Max-Min Diversity Problem (MMDP / discrete p-dispersion), extracted FurthestPoint study package can depended CRAN packages (e.g. TreeSearch). FarFirst(): deterministic farthest-first selection distance matrix, Euclidean coordinates (points =), -demand distance-column oracle (pass column function d, N =) spaces coordinate embedding. default seed runs best--three ensemble "random_furthest" starts (whose pivots drawn session RNG; set seed reproducible selection, supply via pivots argument) keeps best MinDist(). deterministic O(N) anchors ("centroid", "peripheral") costlier O(N²) anchors ("diameter", "anti_medoid", "medoid", "rowsum", "rownorm") available opt-strategies. DropAdd(): DropAdd tabu search (Porumbel et al. 2011); accepts dist object, distance matrix, coordinate matrix (points =). ExactMaxMin(): exact node-packing optimum (Sayyady & Fathi 2016) via highs MILP backend. GraspPR(): GRASP path relinking (Resende et al. 2010), dense-matrix-refinement metaheuristic attains highest T_k package’s methods small medium instances. MinDist(): k-centre objective (minimum pairwise distance). MaxMinSeed(): exposes peripheral seed indices directly.
